conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Marble Run
style.description: A handmade wooden marble machine on a workshop pegboard: glass marbles roll down grooved maple rails and brass wire tracks, spiral through glass funnels, trip flags and brass counters, and collect in jars. Warm upper-left light casts the machine's shadows onto the wall.

sfx.roll: rumble (pitch 3–5 by speed) + faint paper grit

motion: Marbles are the only actors. Each marble's position is a closed-form function of time along pre-authored segments (marbles.js): constant-acceleration rolls, ballistic falls, damped bounces, rebounds, holds.
Rolling rotation is exact: angle = distance / r about up × direction, so the inner swirl visibly rolls.
Every impact in the schedule becomes a sound: glass clacks, wooden knocks, brass tonks; rolls become rumble.
Mechanisms react only to marble events: gates drop, flags trip, counters roll their drums, tags swing on their hooks (damped pendulum).
Camera: frontal, slow tracking pans that follow the lead marble, slight parallax; no orbits.

objects.procedural: tempered-hardboard pegboard 20 × 12 m at z = 0: hole grid 0.3 m, hand-painted red arrows
walnut workbench top (planks) at y = 0, 1.7 m deep, with a front apron

notes.mechanism: Every marble's position/rotation is MarblePlan.at(t) from marbles.js: closed-form segments (constant-acceleration rolls, ballistic falls, damped bounces, rebounds, coupled push). SCORE = scoreFromEvents(plan events) + counter ticks at the flag crossings.
